caseno: Appeal from Appellate Order No. 8 of 1977.
lawyer:
Md. Ansar Ali ----- For the Appellant.

Vs.

full_judgment: This second Miscellaneous appeal arises out of the lower appellate court affirming an order 1 of the trial Court dismissing a Miscellaneous case under section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure objecting to the execution of a com-promise decree passed in suit for declaration of title and recovery of possession of a disputed land. The main ground for objection was that the second term of compromise as contained in the solenama, Ext. A was not complied with by the plaintiff decree-holder and in such circumstances the compromise decree could not be put into execution. In accordance with the provision of solenama pursuant to the compromise decree which was passed by the trial court, the plaintiff decree-holder was obliged to execute a document within a given time in favour of the defendant-judgment debtor transferring a portion of the suit land as specified in the solenama itself. Admittedly, without complying with the terms of the solenama the plaintiff-decree holder put the compromise decree into execution when the defendant judgment debtor objected thereto on that ground. The courts below dismissed the objection of the defendant judgment-debtor mainly on the ground that the executing court could not go beyond the decree as such. In a decree passed by a court on com-promise between the parties concerned where-in the terms of the compromise have been made as part of the decree, the executing court is obliged to see whether the terms of compromise have been complied with by the party concerned while executing the decree. The courts below in overlooking such omission on the part of the plaintiff decree holder evidently erred in dismissing the defendant-judgment debtor's objection to the execution case. For these reasons the judgment of the Sub-ordinate Judge of Kushtia passed on 9th November, 1966 in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 14 of 1966 affirming order No. 8 dated 6-4-66 passed by the second Munsif of Kushtia in Miscellaneous case No. 100 of 1965 arising out of Title Execution case No. 42 of 1965 is set-aside. The defendant judgment debtors objection under section 47 CPC is hereby allowed. The plaintiff-decree holder is, however, granted further time to comply with its obligation to transfer the agreed part of the suit land to the defendant judgment debtor by a registered deed of conveyance as referred to in the second term of the petition of compromise, Ext. A within two months from depositing the registration costs and stamp duty by the defendant judgment debtor before the executing court. The defendant judgment debtor shall deposit registration costs and stamp duty before the executing court within two months from the arrival of the records of this case along with the order of the court. If the defendant judgment debtor fails to deposit the registration fee and stamp duty, etc within the given time, the execution case shall proceed as usual against him. Even if after depositing the registration cost and stamp duty by the defendant-judgment debtor before the executing court. The plaintiff decree-holder fails to execute and register the deed of conveyance within the given time, as mentioned herein before, the execution case shall stand dismissed.
